Subject: Request: DPA + subprocessor list and EU transfer evidence

Hi Dylan,

We're kicking off legal review for a small pilot and need the following to complete our privacy review and procurement checklist: 

- Current DPA template you prefer (PDF or Docx)
- Complete subprocessor matrix with countries of processing and purposes
- Confirmation of transfer mechanism for EU data (SCCs, DPF, or other) and any attestation you can provide for subprocessors located in APAC/India
- Preferred e-sign provider (DocuSign vs AdobeSign) so our procurement team can route the PO

We'd like to close this by EOD next week if possible. Please loop in your privacy counsel where helpful.

Thanks,
Marta Ortega
Legal Operations | Argus Health
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ortega <marta.ortega@argushealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: DPA + subprocessor list and EU transfer evidence

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our standard DPA and the current subprocessor matrix (see filenames below). Quick answers up front:

- Transfer mechanism: Redwood executes SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) as our baseline. We maintain an internal EU addendum and can support customers on Dedicated/Private deployments for EU data residency when requested.
- Subprocessor attestation: we can provide a signed attestation letter confirming compliance controls for subprocessors, including those based in India — we'll have privacy produce that once scope is agreed.
- E-sign: we prefer DocuSign by default; we can also accommodate AdobeSign if your procurement requires it.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.2.pdf, subprocessor_matrix_20260512.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm which signatures we should expect (Marta + procurement contact + PO number).
2) We produce the attestation PDF and upload a DocuSign envelope if you prefer e-sign.
3) Legal to review any redlines returned to me; we'll coordinate internal sign-off.

Looping Neha (privacy) for the attestation and Karthik for procurement coordination.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marta Ortega <marta.ortega@argushealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@argushealth.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: DPA + subprocessor list and EU transfer evidence

Thanks Dylan — procurement looped in (procurement@argushealth.com). Our procurement lead is Steve Hall; he prefers DocuSign but can accept AdobeSign if necessary.

A couple clarifying asks from our side:
- Can the attestation explicitly list which subprocessors process PHI or sensitive health data? We need to map vendor risk.
- Does Redwood offer KMS/HSM options for Dedicated or Private customers? If so, can that be reflected in the DPA (or an addendum)?

We aim to have a signed DPA + PO in place before the pilot start (target week of May 24).

Best,
Marta
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Argus Health — subprocessor attestation / DPA redlines (internal)

Dylan/Karthik,

Notes for Argus:
- We can provide a signed Subprocessor Attestation that enumerates subprocessors, locations, and whether they handle PHI/sensitive categories. Mark as "Attestation A" (separate one-page PDF) so it doesn't enlarge the DPA itself.
- Transfer mechanism: SCCs are fine; if Argus requires DPF/DPF reliance, flag it — currently we rely on SCCs + technical controls.
- KMS/HSM: available for Private and Dedicated customers; for Hosted we provide customer-managed keys only via KMS integrations for enterprise tiers. Add a short addendum template referencing KMS options.
- Redlines to watch: audit rights (limit scope to subset of logs), retention periods (align to product defaults but allow project-level adjustments), and indemnity carve-outs tied to third-party subprocessors.

I'll draft the attestation and the KMS addendum. Dylan, you can share the DocuSign envelope once procurement confirms signer list.

-Neha
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
